title: Company-wide policies and process documentation
author: Avery Chen
content:
Summary:
This document centralizes Redwood Inference's company-wide policies and core operational processes: access & permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expenses, vendor management, travel policies, and internal templates. It is intended as the canonical reference for policy owners, approvers, and contributors.

1) Introduction
Purpose: Provide a single, consistent set of rules, approval flows, and templates used across the company. Scope: Applies to all employees, contractors, and vendors interacting with Redwood systems or incurring company spend. Exceptions must be routed via Risk & Exceptions (security-and-compliance).
Owners and escalation paths:
- Primary owner: People Ops (people-ops)
- Security owner: Security & Compliance (security-and-compliance)
- Finance owner: Finance & Legal (finance-legal)
- Operational questions: eng-platform
Contact: policies@redwoodinference.com (people-ops)

2) Access & Permissions
Short intro: Access is provisioned on the principle of least privilege, using role-based groups and automated access reviews. Core systems: Okta (SSO), AWS IAM, GCP IAM, HashiCorp Vault, GitHub (org), JIRA, Confluence.
Access model and roles:
- Role types: admin, engineer, product, finance, read-only, contractor
- Approvals: People Ops + Team Lead required for persistent elevated access (admin or cross-account).
Provisioning workflow (standard requests):
1. Employee joins -> People Ops creates Okta user and assigns base group (engineering/product/go-to-market).
2. Team lead files access request in /jira/bds-access with target resource and justification.
3. People Ops and resource owner approve; automations grant group membership.
4. Access is logged via audit-logging service (auditlog.redwoodinference.com).
Periodic review and recertification:
- Quarterly automated access reviews by team leads for all admin and privileged groups.
- Contractors: 30-, 60-, and 90-day access expirations depending on contract term.
Privileged access exceptions and emergency access:
- Emergency (break-glass) process: on-call SRE may request temporary access via PagerDuty incident channel; emergency grants are time-limited (max 8 hours) and require post-incident justification within 24 hours.
Access control matrix (example table):
Resource | Role | Default Access | Approval Required | Owner
--- | --- | --- | --- | ---
Production S3 buckets | engineer | read-only | Cross-team admin approval | eng-infra
Production infra (Terraform apply) | admin | no | People Ops + Infra Lead | eng-infra
Secrets (Vault) | admin | per-role | Security review | security-and-compliance
Confluence spaces | product | edit | Space owner | eng-developer-experience

3) Change Management
Purpose: Minimize service disruption and document changes to production systems. Applies to infra, runtime, models served, and critical config.
Change categories:
- Standard: low-risk, pre-approved routine changes (e.g., staggered config updates).
- Normal: changes requiring scheduled maintenance window and approval (e.g., runtime config, model rollout).
- Emergency: unplanned fixes to mitigate degradation or security incidents.
Change request process (normal change):
1. Submit Change Request in CHG board (JIRA type: Change) with description, rollback plan, test plan, blast radius, and risk level.
2. Change Advisory Board (CAB) review for changes with >1 hour expected downtime or cross-service impact. CAB members: eng-sre, eng-platform, security, product representatives.
3. Schedule during maintenance window (Mon-Fri 02:00-06:00 UTC preferred for infra; product changes schedule per product owner).
4. Execute with runbook and monitoring dashboards; verify post-change health checks.
Rollback criteria:
- Define explicit rollback triggers (error rate >2x baseline for 10 minutes, latency >200ms above SLO, or failed smoke tests).
Emergency changes:
- Follow incident process; document change and RCA within 72 hours. All emergency changes reviewed in next CAB meeting.
Change metrics and SLOs:
- Target: 95% of normal changes have completed post-change verification within 24 hours.
- Audit: all changes retained in JIRA with links to runbooks and monitoring dashboards.

4) Data Management
Classification levels:
- Public: no access controls required.
- Internal: default for internal docs, retained per internal retention rules.
- Confidential: PII, customer data, model inputs with customer PII.
- Restricted: regulated data (e.g., health/financial data), requires encryption-at-rest and dedicated private deployment if necessary.
Data handling rules:
- Encryption: All Confidential and Restricted data must be encrypted at rest (KMS) and in transit (TLS 1.2+). Use customer-managed keys (CMK) in Vault for Private deployments.
- Access: Principle of least privilege; dataset access requires explicit data owner approval and documented purpose.
- Retention: Default retention for Internal documents = 3 years; Confidential datasets follow contractual obligations (common windows: 1, 3, 7 years).
- Backups: Daily encrypted backups for production datasets; weekly restore tests.
Data transfer and export controls:
- Exports of Confidential/Restricted data require Data Protection review (security-and-compliance + legal).
- Cross-border transfers must follow data residency guidance and be approved by legal.
Data incident and breach response:
- Follow security incident response runbook (security-and-compliance). Notify CISO and legal within 24 hours of confirmed breach.

5) Procurement & Expenses
Procurement principals: transparency, competitive bidding for >$50k, and segregation of duties.
Approval thresholds and flows:
- <$1,000: individual manager approval.
- $1,000 - $10,000: Department head approval + PO required.
- $10,000 - $50,000: Procurement team + Finance review.
- >$50,000: Competitive quotes (3 preferred) + Finance VP + Legal sign-off.
Procurement steps:
1. Create purchase request in procurement tool (ProcureFlow). Include business justification, cost center, and vendor contact.
2. Procurement team validates vendor, payment terms, and tax forms (W-9 / W-8).
3. Legal reviews contracts for >$10k purchases or where IP/data access is involved.
Expense policy (travels & reimbursements):
- Use company card where possible. Receipts required for all expenses >$25.
- Mileage reimbursed at IRS standard rate (or local equivalent for non-US).
- Per diem for travel: see Travel policy section below.
- Expense submission timeline: within 30 days of expense. Missing receipts may be denied.
Preferred vendors and payment terms:
- Standard supplier list maintained by Procurement (linked in related_pages). Net-30 is default; exceptions require Finance approval.

6) Vendor Management
Vendor onboarding checklist:
1. Procurement request and PO created.
2. Security questionnaire (standardized vendor security checklist) completed for any vendor with access to sensitive data or systems.
3. Legal review and contracting (NDA + Master Services Agreement as appropriate).
4. Technical onboarding: least-privilege access, monitoring, and contact escalation list.
Vendor risk levels and controls:
- Low risk: marketing tools, office supplies - standard contract.
- Medium risk: SaaS with access to internal metadata - require security review and periodic audits.
- High risk: vendors with access to customer data or infra - require SOC2/ISO27001 evidence, penetration test results, and quarterly reviews.
Contract renewals and offboarding:
- Alerts 90/60/30 days before contract end.
- Offboarding checklist: revoke credentials, remove integrations, retain contract/archive per retention policy.

7) Travel Policies
Booking and approval:
- Domestic travel: manager approval required.
- International travel: manager + People Ops approval; travel risk assessment for sensitive locations.
- Book through company travel vendor (Travelly) for preferred rates.
Accommodation and per diem:
- Use business or economy-plus class for flights under 8 hours; business class requires VP approval.
- Per diem is provided per country; refer to Travelly per-diem table.
Expense limits and receipts:
- Hotel, meals, ground transport allowed. Luxury upgrades not reimbursable without pre-approval.
- Submit expenses within 10 business days of return.
Safety and compliance:
- International travel requiring visa/health checks: coordinate with People Ops; company will reimburse necessary vaccinations.

8) Internal Templates and Examples
This section contains canonical templates. Stores are in Confluence template library and attachments. Examples below should be copied into Confluence templates.
- Access request template (use as JIRA change request body):
  *Title:* Access request - [Resource] - [Employee name]
  *Justification:* [Business reason]
  *Requested access:* [role/group]
  *Approvals needed:* [team lead, People Ops]\n
- Change Request template (JIRA CHG):
  *Summary:* [Short description]
  *Service impacted:* [service-name]
  *Change window:* [start - end UTC]
  *Rollback plan:* [commands / steps]
  *Validation plan:* [smoke tests, dashboards]
  *Approvals:* [CAB/approvers]\n
- Vendor security questionnaire (short form):
  1. Do you have SOC 2/ISO27001? (Y/N)
  2. Do you encrypt customer data at rest and in transit? (Y/N)
  3. Do you subcontract data processing? List subprocessors.
  4. Contact for security incidents and SLA for response.

9) Governance, Exceptions and Continuous Improvement
- Policy review cadence: Annual full review by People Ops with security & finance input. High-risk areas (data, access) reviewed semi-annually.
- Exception process: Submit exception request to risk-and-exceptions with business justification, duration, and compensating controls. Exceptions >90 days need executive sponsor.
- Metrics tracked: number of access recertification failures, change rollback rate, procurement cycle time, vendor security score.

10) Appendix: Key contacts and links
- People Ops: people-ops@redwoodinference.com
- Security & Compliance: security@redwoodinference.com
- Procurement: procurement@redwoodinference.com
- Finance: finance@redwoodinference.com
